source.title: Incremental Trainable Parameter Selection in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Anshul Thakur; V. Abrol; Pulkit Sharma; Ting-Ting Zhu; D. Clifton

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates dropout and other regularization methods on held-out performance, but does not compare dropout with training without dropout.
record.gate_note: The paper reports dropout results alongside other regularizers. It does not report random-label experiments, width sweeps, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, or magnitude-aware sharpness against the training–test gap. Hessian-trace observations are not measurements of the magnitude-aware measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The study uses dropout and other regularizers as performance baselines for ITPS. It provides no matched dropout-versus-no-dropout comparison establishing V6, and its experiments do not test the other versions. Hessian trace is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that incrementally selecting trainable parameters induces useful regularization and improves prediction scores across their evaluated tasks and architectures. They acknowledge sensitivity to thresholds and additional memory requirements.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates a new parameter-selection regularizer and compares it with dropout and other regularizers; does not reproduce the claim versions' experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that ITPS outcomes vary with its threshold range and supervision level.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables III–XIV compare held-out performance of ITPS, dropout, and other regularizers. These comparisons do not isolate the benefit of adding standard dropout. ITPS plus spectral dropout evaluates a different intervention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ITPS and its combination with spectral dropout outperform the tested regularization baselines in the evaluated settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Section IV and Figure 4 report low late-training Hessian trace for both Adam and ITPS, alongside training loss and validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam and ITPS reach regions with low Hessian trace in the tested Fashion MNIST network.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: Dropout is not compared with an otherwise identical model trained without dropout, so its standalone effect on held-out error cannot be determined from these results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: reported dropout measurements compare it with other regularization methods, not with a no-dropout baseline needed to establish V6's stated effect.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning; ITPS wrapping Adam is not this comparison.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.

The effect of adding standard dropout relative to otherwise matched training without dropout, including small-data and excessive-dropout regimes and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The empty result-row set is appropriate for these claim versions. The absence of a matched no-dropout control makes V6 untested, rather than absent or challenged.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
The study reports dropout performance against other regularizers, but does not provide an unregularized comparison that isolates whether adding dropout lowers test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
